newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open mixed, eye on five-year auction.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open mixed, eye on five-year auction.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened mixed in quiet trade on Wednesday with market participants largely focused on the afternoon auction of C$2.6 billion in five-year Government of Canada bonds, analysts said.

"The immediate thing is the supply in both (Canadian and U.S.) markets today and tomorrow in the U.S.," said a Toronto-based bond trader with one bank-owned brokerage. "Right now it's starting off pretty quiet."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.09 to C$110.10 to yield 7.140 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 6/32 to yield 7.01 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to 13 basis points from 11 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.

Results of the auction of C$2.6 billion of 5.5 percent Government of Canada bonds due September 1, 2002 will be released at 1315 EDT/1715 GMT. The Bank of Canada will buy at least C$390 million of the new bonds.
Investors are also looking ahead to a U.S. two-year note auction this afternoon and a five-year note auction tomorrow, analysts said.

"The long Canada on a technical basis is back to neutral," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "We've had enough price concessions that today's auctions in the U.S. and Canada should be fairly healthy."
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.07 to C$102.65 to yield 6.62 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond traded unchanged to yield 6.79 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to 17 basis points from 19 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.01 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.17 percent.
